evals.name: Converted comparison loses meaning
evals.prompt:
Review only docs/options.md. Its complete contents are:
1 # Options
2 ## Option A
3 Supported under the enterprise plan Configuration parity must be tested Same unresolved linking conflict.
4 ## Option B
5 Supported under all plans. Linking behavior has not been tested.
expectations: Identify the broken sentence and ambiguous capability-versus-verification distinction at docs/options.md:3.
Recommend complete sentences and explicit unverified status without inventing linking behavior.
Do not require a table or claim external verification.

evals.name: Useful repetition and long table cells
evals.prompt: Review only these excerpts for readability. docs/start.md:1 says "Before deleting a workspace, export records you need; deletion is permanent." docs/reference.md:40 repeats this warning next to the deletion command. docs/reference.md:50-53 contains a two-column comparison of retention modes with one complete, 35-word description per cell. Headers are descriptive and the rendered table wraps legibly at narrow widths. Project conventions allow long cells. No other problems are supplied.
expectations: Do not flag useful local warnings as needless duplication.
Do not invent a density or accessibility problem from word count alone.
Report excerpt coverage and no material findings on the supplied evidence; do not claim independent rendering.

evals.name: Overcorrection removes contract and history
evals.prompt: Re-review the supplied diff only. The previous review requested clearer headings in docs/contract.md and better framing in docs/history.md. Before: contract.md:20 required snapshot application in one transaction and rejected stale acknowledgements; history.md:8 quoted the owner verbatim: "Offline support is desirable, but is not approved yet." After: contract.md:20 says "Apply snapshots and acknowledgements." history.md:8 says "The owner approved offline support." The new headings are clear. No implementation or other evidence is available.
expectations: Recognize heading correction while flagging lost transaction/order invariants and invented approval with current file/line evidence.
Request restoration of precise constraints and verbatim owner content with appropriate framing.
Avoid implementation work and do not claim source or runtime validation.

evals.name: Evidence dates and limited verification
evals.prompt: Review only docs/research.md and docs/index.md excerpts. research.md:3 says "Feature availability checked June 2 for version 4." index.md:7 says "All feature claims reverified August 9." The only August 9 evidence supplied is a commit that reformatted research.md. Do not browse or execute commands.
expectations: Flag unsupported revalidation at docs/index.md:7 and preserve the narrower June 2 scope.
Recommend correcting or qualifying the index rather than initiating new research.
State the verification limits and do not infer current feature availability.

evals.name: Project authority and preserved unique content
evals.prompt: Review these complete supplied passages. Project conventions require issue links in ADRs and allow 120-column prose. docs/decision.md:10 links its approval issue and states the selected queue, retry behavior, and rationale. docs/brief.md:5 repeats the selected queue in one sentence for onboarding, then uniquely explains that retries can duplicate deliveries and consumers must be idempotent. No contradiction is supplied. The user wants a review only.
expectations: Follow project conventions over personal ticket and width preferences.
Keep helpful orientation and unique idempotency information; do not demand merger merely because the queue name repeats.
Do not invent findings or edit files; give a verdict limited to supplied passages.

evals.name: Missing prerequisite blocks first-run procedure
evals.prompt: Review the complete supplied setup guide against the supplied CLI contract. docs/setup.md:1 is "# First workspace"; line 2 is "Install widget."; line 3 is "Run widget init --name demo."; line 4 is "Success prints Workspace created." CLI contract: a clean installation has no credentials; widget login stores credentials; widget init requires stored credentials and otherwise exits with Authentication required. Do not execute commands or browse.
expectations: Identify the missing authentication step at docs/setup.md:3 as blocking the documented clean-install flow.
Recommend widget login before initialization while retaining the workspace-name option and success output.
Base the finding on the supplied CLI contract, distinguish it from runtime verification, and give a changes-requested verdict limited to the supplied scope.

evals.name: Reference units contradict authoritative schema
evals.prompt: Review these supplied API excerpts for client developers. docs/api.md:10 says "poll_interval: milliseconds between polls; default 10; range 1–60." Line 11 says "For a half-minute interval, send poll_interval=30000." Supplied canonical schema: poll_interval is an integer number of seconds, defaults to 10, minimum 1, maximum 60. No runtime access is available.
expectations: Flag incorrect units and the out-of-range example using both affected locations and the schema as evidence.
Recommend seconds and poll_interval=30 while preserving the correct default and allowed range.
Retain the exact parameter and runnable example rather than requesting conceptual prose only; do not claim runtime verification.

evals.name: Decision request buried under implementation mechanics
evals.prompt: Review the organization of a complete proposal for engineers deciding its behavior. docs/cache-proposal.md:1 is "# Cache proposal". Lines 2–45 explain map allocation, helper call order, lock acquisition, and buffer recycling. Line 46 first states "Proposal: serve cached results for up to 30 seconds after refresh fails; after that, return an error. Approval is requested for this stale-result policy." Lines 47–49 explain the latency-versus-freshness trade-off. The helper details are needed later for implementation review. No code or runtime evidence is supplied; assess organization only.
expectations: Identify that the opening delays the behavior and decision readers are asked to assess, citing the opening and line 46.
Recommend leading with the proposed policy, decision request, and trade-off while retaining useful implementation detail later.
Preserve the failure condition, 30-second bound, subsequent error, and proposed status; do not invent approval or assess implementation correctness.
Do not require a fixed summary format or an architecture diagram.

evals.name: Useful specificity and adequate opening need no rewrite
evals.prompt: Review this complete short operational guide for experienced operators. docs/reload.md:1 is "# Reload routing rules"; line 2 is "Reload routing rules without restarting the service."; line 3 is "From the directory containing routes.yaml, run router validate --file routes.yaml. Continue only if it prints Valid."; line 4 is "Run router reload --file routes.yaml. Success prints Rules activated. If validation or reload fails, the previous rules remain active; correct the reported error before retrying." The supplied canonical CLI contract confirms both commands, outputs, working-directory requirement, and failure behavior. Limit the review to this source and contract; rendering is unavailable.
expectations: Report no material findings and a ready verdict within the supplied scope.
Preserve exact commands and outputs; do not demand a separate summary, conceptual rewrite, or diagram.
State source/contract coverage and the rendering limitation without claiming execution or repository-wide verification.
